Medium: [src/validation.js](/Users/justin/code/inbox-e2e-20260308-063405/src/validation.js#L12) builds the summary from `Map` insertion order, so the header changes with the order of the incoming checks (`2 passed, 1 warning` vs `1 warning, 2 passed`). For a human-facing summary, that makes logs and diffs noisier than they need to be. A canonical state order or explicit sort would make the new header easier to scan and compare.
2. Low: [test/validation.test.js](/Users/justin/code/inbox-e2e-20260308-063405/test/validation.test.js#L6) is still named `formats validation checks line by line`, but the function now emits a summary line plus per-check lines. Renaming the test to match the new shape would make failures easier to interpret and keep the change packet self-explanatory.

Open questions or assumptions
- I did not find any in-repo callers besides the test, so I reviewed this as a local formatting change.

Change summary
- The diff is still easy to inspect as a small packet: one production function change and one matching test update.
- `countsByState` and `summary` are clear enough; the main naming issue is the stale test description.

Verification
- `npm test` passes."}

review_verdicts.summary: Sparse-array input appears to regress from tolerated to crashing, and the added tests do not cover that edge case.
review_verdicts.details_markdown:
## Findings
1. Medium: [`src/validation.js#L8`](/Users/justin/code/inbox-e2e-20260308-063405/src/validation.js#L8) now iterates with `for...of`, which can visit sparse-array holes as `undefined`. That means `formatValidationChecks([, { label: 'browser smoke', state: 'warning' }])` can throw when it reads `check.state`, whereas the prior `map`-based implementation skipped holes.
2. Medium: [`test/validation.test.js#L6`](/Users/justin/code/inbox-e2e-20260308-063405/test/validation.test.js#L6) only covers dense arrays, so the regression is not protected by the new test coverage.

## Assumptions
- This review assumes sparse arrays were valid input because the previous implementation tolerated them.
- There are no in-repo caller tests showing whether downstream consumers expect the new leading summary line.

review_verdicts.summary: The packet is small and cohesive, but the new summary header is order-sensitive and one test name no longer describes the behavior clearly.
review_verdicts.details_markdown:
## Comments
1. Medium: [`src/validation.js#L12`](/Users/justin/code/inbox-e2e-20260308-063405/src/validation.js#L12) renders summary counts in `Map` insertion order, so equivalent inputs can produce different header ordering depending on which state appears first. A canonical state order or explicit sort would make logs and diffs easier to compare.
2. Low: [`test/validation.test.js#L6`](/Users/justin/code/inbox-e2e-20260308-063405/test/validation.test.js#L6) is still named `formats validation checks line by line`, even though the function now emits a summary line plus detailed lines. Renaming it would make failures easier to interpret.

## Scope notes
- I did not find evidence of an open PR or broader in-repo callers, so I treated this as a local formatting change with limited external validation context.
